CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern both domestically and internationally, given their vulnerable position as victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of the City of Probolinggo is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and lastly by Law Number 17 of 2016, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Violence against women and children is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The large number of cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, and environment in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT) which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's and Children's Empowerment (P2TP2A), Safe House, Child Social Protection House (RPSA), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc. Which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Article 41

(1) The organization of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be carried out by the Center for Protection Services for Women and Children as an integrated Service Center to provide protection, handling and fulfillment of the rights of victims of violence.

(2) The Service Center as referred to in paragraph (1) is an implementing unit under the coordination of the Agency and is an integrated technical service unit that functions as an information center for women and children, a service center for women and children victims of violence as well as an empowerment center for women and children.

(3) The organization of protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:

a. providing fast and free services to victims; b. organizing complaint services, consultation, mediation, outreach, health, social rehabilitation, spiritual guidance, assistance, enforcement and legal aid, repatriation, social reintegration;
c. cooperating with certain institutions in providing interpreters and volunteer companions required for victims; d. networking with government or private hospitals for treatment and health recovery of victims and cooperating with witness and victim protection institutions, social protection houses or trauma centers owned by the government, community or other institutions for health recovery of victims;
e. providing convenience, comfort and safety for victims; f. maintaining confidentiality of victims; and
g. providing fulfillment of legal aid for victims.
(4) The institutional structure of the Center for Protection Services for Women and children may be upgraded to a structural institution in the form of a Technical Implementation Unit of the Agency (UPTD) as long as it meets the criteria and requirements for the establishment of a Technical Implementation Unit of the Agency according to the provisions of the Minister of Home Affairs Regulation.

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern both domestically and internationally, given their vulnerable position as victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of the City of Probolinggo is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and lastly by Law Number 17 of 2016, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Violence against women and children is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The large number of cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, and environment in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT) which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's and Children's Empowerment (P2TP2A), Safe House, Child Social Protection House (RPSA), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc. Which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Article 41

(3) The organization of protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:

a. providing fast and free services to victims; b. organizing complaint services, consultation, mediation, outreach, health, social rehabilitation, spiritual guidance, assistance, enforcement and legal aid, repatriation, social reintegration;
c. cooperating with certain institutions in providing interpreters and volunteer companions required for victims; d. networking with government or private hospitals for treatment and health recovery of victims and cooperating with witness and victim protection institutions, social protection houses or trauma centers owned by the government, community or other institutions for health recovery of victims;
e. providing convenience, comfort and safety for victims; f. maintaining confidentiality of victims; and
g. providing fulfillment of legal aid for victims.
(4) The institutional structure of the Center for Protection Services for Women and children may be upgraded to a structural institution in the form of a Technical Implementation Unit of the Agency (UPTD) as long as it meets the criteria and requirements for the establishment of a Technical Implementation Unit of the Agency according to the provisions of the Minister of Home Affairs Regulation.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern both domestically and internationally, given their vulnerable position as victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of the City of Probolinggo is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and lastly by Law Number 17 of 2016, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Violence against women and children is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The large number of cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, and environment in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT) which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's and Children's Empowerment (P2TP2A), Safe House, Child Social Protection House (RPSA), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc. Which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 5

The regional government is obliged to implement policies, programs and activities for the protection of women, which can be carried out through efforts to:

a. provide and facilitate women's protection services; b. develop a women's protection data system;
c. implement coordination of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for women's protection among Regional Apparatus; and
d. cooperate with the business world, non-governmental institutions, private companies, Foundations, and other domestic institutions as well as international institutions, in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 41

(1) The organization of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be carried out by the Center for Protection Services for Women and Children as an integrated Service Center to provide protection, handling and fulfillment of the rights of victims of violence.

(2) The Service Center as referred to in paragraph (1) is an implementing unit under the coordination of the Agency and is an integrated technical service unit that functions as an information center for women and children, a service center for women and children victims of violence as well as an empowerment center for women and children.

(3) The organization of protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:

a. providing fast and free services to victims; b. organizing complaint services, consultation, mediation, outreach, health, social rehabilitation, spiritual guidance, assistance, enforcement and legal aid, repatriation, social reintegration;
c. cooperating with certain institutions in providing interpreters and volunteer companions required for victims; d. networking with government or private hospitals for treatment and health recovery of victims and cooperating with witness and victim protection institutions, social protection houses or trauma centers owned by the government, community or other institutions for health recovery of victims;
e. providing convenience, comfort and safety for victims; f. maintaining confidentiality of victims; and
g. providing fulfillment of legal aid for victims.
(4) The institutional structure of the Center for Protection Services for Women and children may be upgraded to a structural institution in the form of a Technical Implementation Unit of the Agency (UPTD) as long as it meets the criteria and requirements for the establishment of a Technical Implementation Unit of the Agency according to the provisions of the Minister of Home Affairs Regulation.
(5) Further provisions regarding the establishment, institutional structure, procedures and mechanisms for organizing the Center for protection services for Women and children Victims of violence shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 29

Regional Government must provide special protection for children in conflict with the law including children in conflict with the law and child victims of criminal acts, in cooperation with the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Courts, institutions/organizations concerned with women and children, parents, families and communities.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Probolinggo City.
2. Regional Government is the Probolinggo City Government.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Probolinggo.
4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Regional Government. 5. Agency is the Agency for Empowerment, Protection of Women and Children and Family Planning of Probolinggo City.
6. Technical Implementation Unit of the Women and Children Protection Agency hereinafter referred to as UPTD PPA is the Technical Implementation Unit of the Women and Children Protection Agency of Probolinggo City.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, family, advocates, police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women and Children will or has occurred.
11. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to strive and work independently after they are restored and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
12. Medical Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical and psychological health so that victims can perform their role again properly and appropriately both in the family and in society.
13. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to perform their social functions appropriately.
14. Repatriation is the effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
15. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
16. Women and Children Protection Service Center, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various forms of discrimination and violence, including trafficking in persons.
17. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, family, advocates, police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women and Children will or has occurred.

g. providing fulfillment of legal aid for victims.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern both domestically and internationally, given their vulnerable position as victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and state. Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Probolinggo City.
2. Regional Government is the Probolinggo City Government.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Probolinggo.
4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Regional Government. 5. Agency is the Agency for Empowerment, Protection of Women and Children and Family Planning of Probolinggo City.
6. Technical Implementation Unit of the Women and Children Protection Agency hereinafter referred to as UPTD PPA is the Technical Implementation Unit of the Women and Children Protection Agency of Probolinggo City.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, family, advocates, police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women and Children will or has occurred.
11. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to strive and work independently after they are restored and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
12. Medical Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical and psychological health so that victims can perform their role again properly and appropriately both in the family and in society.
13. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to perform their social functions appropriately.
14. Repatriation is the effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
15. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
16. Women and Children Protection Service Center, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various forms of discrimination and violence, including trafficking in persons.
17. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.

Article 41

(1) The organization of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be carried out by the Center for Protection Services for Women and Children as an integrated Service Center to provide protection, handling and fulfillment of the rights of victims of violence.

(2) The Service Center as referred to in paragraph (1) is an implementing unit under the coordination of the Agency and is an integrated technical service unit that functions as an information center for women and children, a service center for women and children victims of violence as well as an empowerment center for women and children.

(3) The organization of protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:

a. providing fast and free services to victims; b. organizing complaint services, consultation, mediation, outreach, health, social rehabilitation, spiritual guidance, assistance, enforcement and legal aid, repatriation, social reintegration;
c. cooperating with certain institutions in providing interpreters and volunteer companions required for victims; d. networking with government or private hospitals for treatment and health recovery of victims and cooperating with witness and victim protection institutions, social protection houses or trauma centers owned by the government, community or other institutions for health recovery of victims;
e. providing convenience, comfort and safety for victims; f. maintaining confidentiality of victims; and
g. providing fulfillment of legal aid for victims.
(4) The institutional structure of the Center for Protection Services for Women and children may be upgraded to a structural institution in the form of a Technical Implementation Unit of the Agency (UPTD) as long as it meets the criteria and requirements for the establishment of a Technical Implementation Unit of the Agency according to the provisions of the Minister of Home Affairs Regulation.
(5) Further provisions regarding the establishment, institutional structure, procedures and mechanisms for organizing the Center for protection services for Women and children Victims of violence shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 42

(1) In providing integrated services to women and children victims of violence, UPTD PPA shall carry out all processes necessary for women and children, especially for the fulfillment of victims' rights as referred to in Article 41 paragraph (3) letter b.

(2) In the case of integrated services for women and children victims of violence networked with other institutions, UPTD PPA shall carry out all referral processes necessary for women and children so that they remain protected and their rights are fulfilled.

Article 49

(1) The Agency shall carry out monitoring to ensure synergy, balance and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, activities, protection of Women and children.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Agency to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and children.

(3) Monitoring shall be conducted regularly on Regional Apparatus implementing policies, activities for the protection of Women and children victims of violence.

(4) Monitoring shall be conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children every year.

Article 25

Neglect as referred to in Article 21 letter d is caused by: a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of the child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;

c. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or

d. acts that result in economic dependency by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Article 54

(1) In the implementation of Protection for Women and children, the community may participate to:

a. establish family partners and complaint services at the Kelurahan level by the community;
b. conduct socialization of women's and children's rights independently; c. provide first aid to victims; and
d. report to the competent authority if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, private sector and/or mass media.

Article 29

Regional Government must provide special protection for children in conflict with the law including children in conflict with the law and child victims of criminal acts, in cooperation with the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Courts, institutions/organizations concerned with women and children, parents, families and communities.

Sufficiently Clear.

Sufficiently Clear.

Letter a

What is meant by "health service" is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. What is meant by "rapid" is immediate action taken without complications or simplified procedures. What is meant by "free of charge" is service delivery and accompaniment activities carried out by the Service Center are not charged to the victim.

Letter b

What is meant by "social rehabilitation" is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions properly.

Paragraph (4)

Sufficiently Clear.

Article 3

Community responsibility is implemented in the form of:

(1) preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children; and (2) providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties.

Article 26

Exploitation as referred to in Article 21 letter e is caused by: a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;

b. acts with or without the consent of the victim including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or

c. any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

Article 4

b. provision of services for women victims of violence; and c. strengthening the institutional capacity of women's protection service provider institutions.

a. provide and facilitate women's protection services; b. develop a women's protection data system;
c. implement coordination of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for women's protection among Regional Apparatus; and
d. cooperate with the business world, non-governmental institutions, private companies, Foundations, and other domestic institutions as well as international institutions, in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 49

(1) The Agency shall carry out monitoring to ensure synergy, balance and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, activities, protection of Women and children.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Agency to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and children.

(3) Monitoring shall be conducted regularly on Regional Apparatus implementing policies, activities for the protection of Women and children victims of violence.

(4) Monitoring shall be conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children every year.

Article 41

(1) The organization of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be carried out by the Center for Protection Services for Women and Children as an integrated Service Center to provide protection, handling and fulfillment of the rights of victims of violence.

(2) The Service Center as referred to in paragraph (1) is an implementing unit under the coordination of the Agency and is an integrated technical service unit that functions as an information center for women and children, a service center for women and children victims of violence as well as an empowerment center for women and children.

(3) The organization of protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:

a. providing fast and free services to victims; b. organizing complaint services, consultation, mediation, outreach, health, social rehabilitation, spiritual guidance, assistance, enforcement and legal aid, repatriation, social reintegration;
c. cooperating with certain institutions in providing interpreters and volunteer companions required for victims; d. networking with government or private hospitals for treatment and health recovery of victims and cooperating with witness and victim protection institutions, social protection houses or trauma centers owned by the government, community or other institutions for health recovery of victims;
e. providing convenience, comfort and safety for victims; f. maintaining confidentiality of victims; and
g. providing fulfillment of legal aid for victims.
(4) The institutional structure of the Center for Protection Services for Women and children may be upgraded to a structural institution in the form of a Technical Implementation Unit of the Agency (UPTD) as long as it meets the criteria and requirements for the establishment of a Technical Implementation Unit of the Agency according to the provisions of the Minister of Home Affairs Regulation.
(5) Further provisions regarding the establishment, institutional structure, procedures and mechanisms for organizing the Center for protection services for Women and children Victims of violence shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Community responsibility is implemented in the form of:

(1) preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children; and (2) providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Probolinggo City.
2. Regional Government is the Probolinggo City Government.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Probolinggo.
4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Regional Government. 5. Agency is the Agency for Empowerment, Protection of Women and Children and Family Planning of Probolinggo City.
6. Technical Implementation Unit of the Women and Children Protection Agency hereinafter referred to as UPTD PPA is the Technical Implementation Unit of the Women and Children Protection Agency of Probolinggo City.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, family, advocates, police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women and Children will or has occurred.
11. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to strive and work independently after they are restored and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
12. Medical Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical and psychological health so that victims can perform their role again properly and appropriately both in the family and in society.
13. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to perform their social functions appropriately.
14. Repatriation is the effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
15. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
16. Women and Children Protection Service Center, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various forms of discrimination and violence, including trafficking in persons.
17. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.

Article 57

This Regional Regulation shall come into effect on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by its placement in the Regional Gazette of the City of Probolinggo.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern both domestically and internationally, given their vulnerable position as victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of the City of Probolinggo is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and lastly by Law Number 17 of 2016, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Violence against women and children is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The large number of cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, and environment in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT) which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's and Children's Empowerment (P2TP2A), Safe House, Child Social Protection House (RPSA), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc. Which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

CHAPTER XI

Article 14

(1) The Regional Government shall implement the Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the health field by providing comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb, which is carried out in stages adjusted to the regional financial capacity and supported by community participation.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include:

a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services; and
b. exemption from the burden of health service costs for children in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern both domestically and internationally, given their vulnerable position as victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of the City of Probolinggo is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and lastly by Law Number 17 of 2016, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Violence against women and children is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The large number of cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, and environment in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT) which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's and Children's Empowerment (P2TP2A), Safe House, Child Social Protection House (RPSA), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc. Which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Probolinggo City.
2. Regional Government is the Probolinggo City Government.

8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, family, advocates, police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women and Children will or has occurred.
11. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to strive and work independently after they are restored and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
12. Medical Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical and psychological health so that victims can perform their role again properly and appropriately both in the family and in society.
13. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to perform their social functions appropriately.
14. Repatriation is the effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
15. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
16. Women and Children Protection Service Center, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various forms of discrimination and violence, including trafficking in persons.
17. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.

I. GENERAL

Women and children are a serious concern both domestically and internationally, given their vulnerable position as victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy household life, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of the City of Probolinggo is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 and lastly by Law Number 17 of 2016, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons.

Violence against women and children is a violation of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The large number of cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low levels of economy, education, and environment in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of such violence need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT) which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's and Children's Empowerment (P2TP2A), Safe House, Child Social Protection House (RPSA), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc. Which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government is obliged and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women and children victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 49

(1) The Agency shall carry out monitoring to ensure synergy, balance and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, activities, protection of Women and children.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Agency to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and children.

(3) Monitoring shall be conducted regularly on Regional Apparatus implementing policies, activities for the protection of Women and children victims of violence.

(4) Monitoring shall be conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children every year.

Part Three

Women's Empowerment

Article 50

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and children victims of violence shall be conducted at the end of each Budget year or if necessary according to needs.

(2) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER XI

FUNDING

Article 41

(1) The organization of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be carried out by the Center for Protection Services for Women and Children as an integrated Service Center to provide protection, handling and fulfillment of the rights of victims of violence.

(2) The Service Center as referred to in paragraph (1) is an implementing unit under the coordination of the Agency and is an integrated technical service unit that functions as an information center for women and children, a service center for women and children victims of violence as well as an empowerment center for women and children.

(3) The organization of protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:

a. providing fast and free services to victims; b. organizing complaint services, consultation, mediation, outreach, health, social rehabilitation, spiritual guidance, assistance, enforcement and legal aid, repatriation, social reintegration;
c. cooperating with certain institutions in providing interpreters and volunteer companions required for victims; d. networking with government or private hospitals for treatment and health recovery of victims and cooperating with witness and victim protection institutions, social protection houses or trauma centers owned by the government, community or other institutions for health recovery of victims;
e. providing convenience, comfort and safety for victims; f. maintaining confidentiality of victims; and
g. providing fulfillment of legal aid for victims.
(4) The institutional structure of the Center for Protection Services for Women and children may be upgraded to a structural institution in the form of a Technical Implementation Unit of the Agency (UPTD) as long as it meets the criteria and requirements for the establishment of a Technical Implementation Unit of the Agency according to the provisions of the Minister of Home Affairs Regulation.
(5) Further provisions regarding the establishment, institutional structure, procedures and mechanisms for organizing the Center for protection services for Women and children Victims of violence shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 42

(1) In providing integrated services to women and children victims of violence, UPTD PPA shall carry out all processes necessary for women and children, especially for the fulfillment of victims' rights as referred to in Article 41 paragraph (3) letter b.

(2) In the case of integrated services for women and children victims of violence networked with other institutions, UPTD PPA shall carry out all referral processes necessary for women and children so that they remain protected and their rights are fulfilled.

Part Two

Center for Protection Services for Women and Children

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Probolinggo City.
2. Regional Government is the Probolinggo City Government.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Probolinggo.
4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Regional Government. 5. Agency is the Agency for Empowerment, Protection of Women and Children and Family Planning of Probolinggo City.

7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, family, advocates, police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women and Children will or has occurred.
11. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to strive and work independently after they are restored and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
12. Medical Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical and psychological health so that victims can perform their role again properly and appropriately both in the family and in society.
13. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to perform their social functions appropriately.
14. Repatriation is the effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
15. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
16. Women and Children Protection Service Center, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various forms of discrimination and violence, including trafficking in persons.
17. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.
